components.text: The pro inference requires perfect goodness to make life and moral agency substantially expected.
Whether evidence of intentional structure also warrants benevolent purposes and the divine preference needed for the likelihood claim.
The reductio requires tailored naturalistic explanations to be illegitimate or universally defeating.
The comparison must include the relevant aggregate naturalistic probability rather than one narrow rival.
Whether naturalistic alternatives are merely arbitrary defeaters or members of a relevant aggregate rival hypothesis space.
Whether classical theism has been compared against the full relevant naturalistic alternative space.
The naturalistic-disjunction strategy must avoid making all conceivable theistic evidence evidentially inert.
Whether generating a naturalistic alternative for any observation makes empirical confirmation of theism impossible.
The original Bayesian comparison requires commensurately specified theistic and naturalistic hypothesis spaces.
The universal-defeater objection does not itself define the eligible rival family or comparison granularity.
Whether the relevant issue is universal skepticism or a properly matched comparison between specified families and their disjunctions.
Whether the comparison fixes comparable levels of specificity for theism and naturalism.
The pro side must define the compared theism and the complete eligible naturalistic family.
Naturalistic rivals remain eligible only if consistent with the stipulated single-universe naturalism.
Whether pro has specified both the theistic hypothesis and the naturalistic comparison class at a usable granularity.
Whether the pro claim includes every hypothesis consistent with stipulated single-universe naturalism.
The stipulated restriction must materially narrow the eligible naturalistic hypotheses enough to support the claimed comparison.
Concrete remaining rivals show that the issue is not exhausted by an unrestricted arbitrary-hypothesis strategy.
Whether restricting the comparison to one natural universe materially narrows the available rival explanations.
Theism must predict the relevant intentional evidence better than alternative powerful-agent hypotheses.
Defining perfect-being theism does not by itself determine its probability for a particular religiously infused event.
Whether general theism predicts a particular intentional event once the agent's specific intentions remain unknown.
Whether extraordinary intentional evidence uniquely favors theism rather than several strange agent hypotheses.
The reply must identify an asymmetry between divine and alien intentions rather than merely posit agency.
Perfect goodness is offered as information about divine motives beyond bare intentional agency.
Specific alien rivals tailored to the evidence incur prior-probability costs.
Whether perfect goodness supplies predictive content absent from a general alien hypothesis with opaque intentions.
Whether tailoring a naturalistic agent hypothesis to the observation imposes a corresponding prior-probability cost.
The combined naturalistic alternatives must retain enough prior mass for their evidential fit to undercut theism.
The probability assigned to specific augmented naturalisms must be evaluated within the general naturalistic space.
The mere availability of many naturalistic resources does not show that their predictive subset has substantial prior mass.
Whether the many naturalistic hypotheses that fit fine-tuning collectively occupy substantial conditional probability space.
How probability should be allocated across the full restricted naturalistic family.
The claim of negligible augmented-naturalism mass must account for the breadth of naturalistic scenarios compatible with extraordinary observations.
The availability of alternatives need not make either worldview conclusively ruled in or ruled out.
Even the stipulated naturalistic domain permits broad science-fiction-like mechanisms.
Whether the naturalistic evidence-compatible region is negligibly narrow rather than broadly populated by simulation and science-fiction possibilities.
Whether failure of complete decisiveness is being confused with failure of any probabilistic confirmation.
The simplicity of one unlimited perfect-being hypothesis must be compared with the aggregate prior of all limited alternatives.
A specific limited alternative may be less simple while its full disjunction can still carry greater total probability.
Whether a single simple unlimited hypothesis can receive more intrinsic probability than the disjunction of all finite-limit alternatives.
The claimed prior asymmetry requires a principled weighting of coherence, simplicity, and modesty.
Moving predictive fit into a prior does not settle how competing prior virtues should be weighted.
A defined comparison class still requires justified intrinsic-probability allocation within that class.
Whether coherence and simplicity justify the asserted prior asymmetry between theism and augmented naturalism.
The reply must show that theism retains a relevant prior advantage even after granting the limited-hypothesis disjunction.
The aggregate probability of quasi-theistic alternatives may exceed theism without equalizing theism and augmented naturalism.
Whether uncertainty about limited alternatives eliminates the comparative coherence advantage over augmented naturalism.
Whether conceding greater mass to quasi-theistic alternatives defeats the narrower theism-versus-augmented-naturalism comparison.
Any coherence advantage for theism must be balanced against naturalism's ontological-simplicity advantage.
The intrinsic-probability comparison cannot rely on coherence alone while omitting ontological parsimony.
Whether coherence exhausts intrinsic probability or must be balanced against naturalism's ontological parsimony.
The pro side must explain why naturalism's ontological-simplicity advantage does not overturn the claimed prior asymmetry.
The relative magnitude of coherence and parsimony must be sufficiently justified to resolve the ambiguity.
Whether naturalism's ontological-simplicity advantage defeats the claimed coherence-based probability asymmetry.
The asserted overall balance requires a reliable method for trading coherence against ontological parsimony.
A qualitative coherence advantage does not by itself determine the posterior balance.
Prior and likelihood components cannot settle the comparison if their theoretical-virtue weights remain indeterminate.
Whether coherence, parsimony, and other theoretical virtues can be weighted reliably enough to establish the claimed overall comparison.
The closing must show why an extreme likelihood ratio can dominate unresolved differences in theoretical virtues.
Naturalism's ontological-simplicity advantage is alleged to be swamped by the fine-tuning likelihood ratio.
Coherence is invoked to resist the claim that disjunctive modesty automatically dominates.
The reply supplies an orders-of-magnitude claim intended to overcome qualitative prior ambiguity.
Whether a sufficiently extreme augmented-naturalism likelihood or conditional-share disadvantage can swamp uncertain theoretical-virtue differences.
Whether naturalism's ontological simplicity can outweigh the proposed many-orders-of-magnitude ratio.
The closing's decisive aggregate likelihood and prior claims must be answered to defeat its swamping inference.
The fine-tuning datum may reflect a defect in the physical theory rather than an objective cosmic feature.
Whether the enormous likelihood or conditional-share ratio used in the closing is justified.
Whether apparent fine-tuning is an objective cosmic datum rather than a defect of the physical theory.
The closing requires a non-negligible theistic likelihood or numerator grounded in justified divine psychology.
Perfect goodness must yield a warranted expectation about divine intentions and creative choices.
Knowing that God is good does not automatically settle what goodness means or what God would choose.
Whether perfect goodness provides a justified probability distribution over divine intentions and creative choices.
Whether the numerator in the closing's swamping ratio is non-negligible given uncertain divine psychology.
